subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Scarcity Principle
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Scarcity Principle.

hook.text: When Worchel put cookies in a nearly empty jar, people rated them tastier than identical cookies from a full jar.

buildup.text: Scarcity increases perceived value. When something is rare or running out, we want it more, despite actual quality.

discovery.text: Cialdini identified scarcity as a core persuasion principle. It triggers fear of missing out and accelerates decisions.

twist.text: Artificial scarcity is the marketing version. Limited editions, countdown timers, and low-stock warnings use urgency.

climax.text: When scarcity pressure hits, pause. Ask: do I want this or do I fear losing the option? The distinction saves money.

punchline.text: Scarcity makes you want things you would otherwise skip.

quiz.question: What did Worchel's cookie jar experiment show?
options: People preferred cookies from full jars
People rated scarce cookies as tastier than identical abundant ones
Cookie quality had no effect on preference
